text:
Boston has won four straight, and Hampus Lindholm has been on the ice for a lot of it. The Bruins take almost 60% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with him at five on five, ten points better than without him, and his pairing with Charlie McAvoy has outscored teams 12-3. That pair is the backbone of a 13-4-1 start.

But read the luck column too: Boston has scored 10.9 more goals than its chances deserve with Lindholm on the ice, a huge number. That's shooting luck on Boston's side of the puck. The share is real; the scoreline is inflated. His own offense is quiet: 5 points in 18 games and 1 point in his last ten.

Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking from last season shows the defensive skill: he stops 16% of the entries aimed at him, against 11% typical. Evolving-Hockey had him facing tough competition (94th percentile) but losing ground on penalties. His top speed ranks in the 99th percentile. He played only 14:30 against Florida on Sunday, his lowest of the season, worth watching. We project about 28 points.
headline: Hampus Lindholm's lucky streak
